paste:
SIKA RETARDER® N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika Retarder® N, September 2024, Version 01.04 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sika_retarder_n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika Retarder® N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2024, Version 01.04).
1.2 Product description. Sika Retarder® N is used to retard the setting time of the concrete to allow concreting under conditions of high ambient temperatures and placing of mass concrete. It is designed to be used for pumped, prestressed and structural concrete.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Increases the setting time of concrete
    - Used in high temperatures
    - Excellent for large concrete pours
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika Retarder® N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Re- Set Retarder
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports. Sika Retarder® N meets and exceeds all requirements of Australian Standard 1478.1-2000 for Set-Retarding Admixture (Re)
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Minimises the risk of cold joints.
    - After the initial retardation, the rate of hardening proceeds at a rate equivalent to, or greater than, unretarded normal concrete.
    - Delivery of concrete can be made over long distances from the premix concrete plant.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Aqueous solution of selected carbohydrates
    - Appearance and colour: Cloudy yellow liquid
    - Specific gravity: 1.05 g/cm³ approx.
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Concreting guidance: Concrete should be placed according to good concrete practice and proper curing procedures should take place
    - Specific advice: May slightly increase air content when used with water reducers.
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: Bulk deliveries; 1000 litre IBC; 205 litre drum; 10 litre container
    - Shelf life: Stored at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C in unopened original containers protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is at least one (1) year.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperature between 5°C and 35°C , protected from the direct sunlight

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (September 2024, Version 01.04) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2024, Version 01.04) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Compatibility: Sika Retarder® N is compatible with all the types of Portland cement . When using with other admixtures, check their compatibility first.
4.3 Recommended dosage. The effect of Sika Retarder® N depends on a number of factors such as cement type, ambient temperature and mix design. The optimum dosage should be determined by site or laboratory tests with the particular concrete mix design. The rate of addition is generally in the range of: 200ml ± 100ml per 100kg of cementitious materials. Note: For dose rates higher than 400 ml/100kg please refer to your Sika representative.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations. Increase in dosage rate will cause an increase in the setting time. If this occurs, do not change to an accelerator. A severe overdose may delay the setting time of the concrete to detrimental extent.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (September 2024, Version 01.04) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika Retarder® N, September 2024, Version 01.04, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/4/sika_retarder_n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Retarder N, version 26/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sds-sika-retardern.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: EPD Sika Retarder® N, version 12/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/epd-sika-retardern.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaÂ® Retarder N, https://aus.sika.com/dam/dms/au01/c/sds-sika-retardern.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
